messages.author: 0b90a2764fdb150d
messages.subject: Decreasing resolution cause error in 'maxColorValue'
parts:
Dear all
i have here attached picture and i want to count fruits.
In order to explore correct parameters for field masking i would like to reduce resolution. My code is:

EX1<-stack("./myPathTo/IMG_20190630_192732.jpg")
EX1<-aggregate(EX1, fact= 5)
EX.shapeFile<-fieldPolygon(EX1,extent = T)
EX1.I1<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX1,index = c("SI","BGI","BI"))

par(mfrow=c(1,2))
hist(EX1.I1$BI)
plot(EX1.I1$BI)

EX1.R1<-fieldMask(mosaic = EX1.I1, index = "BI", cropValue = 90, cropAbove = T)

but last command generate here below error
Error in grDevices::rgb(RGB[, 1], RGB[, 2], RGB[, 3], alpha = alpha, max = scale) : 
  invalid value of 'maxColorValue'

If i omit  "EX1<-aggregate(EX1, fact= 5)" it work, even if take a lot of time.

Any hints??
Thanks

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Decreasing resolution cause error in 'maxColorValue'
parts:
Hi there,

 I believe the aggregate function with fact=5 is changing too much your pixel values. 

Did you try to use fact=2 or 3 first?


Otherwise, I guess you will need to rescale your pics to be like 0 to 255. 

But I am not sure how good is this approach: 

NewMosaic<-setValues(mosaic, scales::rescale(values(mosaic), to = c(0, 255))) 

 

I prefer to use fact=2 on the aggregate function.


Please, let me know if these suggestions worked.

 Best,

Filipe

parts:
Hi Massimiliano,

 I was checking the function and I don’t know why for your picture the second plot doesn’t work. I need more time to check on that. But for a fast solution, you can use plot=F on fieldMask(). As soon as I have time to figure it out I will let you know.

 

EX1.R1<-fieldMask(mosaic = EX1.I1, index = "BI", cropValue = 90, cropAbove = T,plot=F) 

plotRGB(EX1.R1$newMosaic)

plot(EX1.R1$mask)

 

All the best,

Filipe
